title: Send the core system's answer, whatever it contains

blocks.text: The core banking system now sends a message for the terminal's screen with every decision, and its new release issues longer approval codes. Since the upgrade, some terminals get no answer at all, and their acquirers reverse purchases the core system approved. The server's log shows a `<send>` for each of them.

`CoreAnswer`, in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/CoreAnswer.java`, turns the core's `Decision` into the response that `SendResponse` sends. The server runs it on several links, and their layouts differ. Finish the two methods marked `TODO`:

items: `packs(...)`: whether a message can go out where the request came from;
`makeSendable(...)`: what to change when it can't.

blocks.text: When you're done, every decision reaches the terminal as close to what the core system said as the link allows. About fifteen lines in total.
The tests put the channel the request came in on into the Context, as `IncomingListener` does, and pack your response with that channel's packager.

cases.says: an approval goes out with the core's approval code and message
a decline goes out with its response code and message and no approval code
an approval code too long for field 38 turns the answer into a sendable 96, without the code that didn't fit
a message too long for field 44 is dropped from a decline, which still goes out, because only packing reveals which field doesn't fit
a message too long for field 44 is dropped and the approval keeps its code
the check uses the packager of the channel the request came in on, so a link whose field 44 is longer keeps the whole message

origin.section: 6.5 `set` Checks Nothing; the Packager Checks After the Vote

concepts: set checks nothing and the packager checks when SendResponse sends, after the vote; a participant packs a copy with the source channel's packager in prepare and answers without the field that didn't fit.
